The African Democratic Congress (ADC), has taken its leadership’s legal challenge to the Court of Appeal, presenting 17 grounds to set aside Justice Peter Lifu’s judgment of November 5, 2026.
The party is also challenging the earlier ruling that allowed Hon. Nafiu Bala Gombe to amend his suit despite ADC’s unresolved objection to the trial court’s jurisdiction.
ADC said it would not accept a judgment whose contents were built on a case the court had no authority to hear.
This was as the factional national chairman of ADC, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has written to the INEC, claiming to assume office as national chairman following the November 5 court order by Justice Peter Lifu.
In a statement issued by the Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, the party said its Notice of Appeal challenged the trial court’s jurisdiction to decide what the ADC maintained was an internal party leadership dispute.
It also questioned the court’s treatment of an earlier Federal High Court judgment on the leadership transition, delivered on 2 July 2026, which the party said had not been set aside.
“The 17 grounds challenge the foundation, findings and orders of Justice Lifu’s judgment. The ADC has asked the Court of Appeal to examine whether the trial court had jurisdiction, whether the claimant had standing, whether disputed evidence was properly assessed, and whether the sweeping orders made against the party can stand in law,” Shaibu said.
In its separate appellant’s brief challenging the ruling of 24 July 2026, the ADC argued that the court granted Gombe leave to amend his originating summons while deferring its decision on the party’s preliminary objection to jurisdiction.
The brief, the ADC said, contended that the motion seeking amendment had altered the description of parties and the capacity in which a defendant was sued without prior leave of court.
‘’That brief was settled by Chief J. S. Okutepa, SAN, lead counsel for the ADC in the appeal against the amendment ruling. It asks the Court of Appeal to set aside the order granting amendment and consider the outstanding jurisdictional objection,” Shuaib stressed.
The ADC has also asked the Court of Appeal for an injunction to prevent the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) from changing the party’s leadership records or interfering with the names and nomination particulars of its presidential and governorship candidates while the appeal is heard.
The party argued that Lifu’s judgment rested on an amended court process that was already under appeal, yet the trial court proceeded to judgment before that appeal was resolved.
It said, If INEC acted on the judgment now, the resulting changes could be difficult to undo and could render a successful appeal meaningless. The party has therefore asked the appellate court to preserve the position that existed before the November 5 judgment.
“These are serious questions before the Court of Appeal. INEC must not make changes that could preempt the court’s decision or put the party’s candidates in jeopardy while our applications are pending.
“We are asking the court to protect the subject of the appeal so that its eventual decision has practical effect,” Shaibu said, adding that it was making its legal challenge public so Nigerians could understand precisely what was before the Court of Appeal.
Shaibu said the party would defend its rights, its leadership and the lawful decisions of its members through the courts.
Accordingly, he maintained that, ‘’No one should use a contested judgment to alter the party’s records or disturb its candidates before the appellate court has had the opportunity to decide the issues placed before it.’’
Factional national chairman of the ADC, Nafiu Bala Gombe, has written to INEC claiming to assume office as national chairman of the party.
This, he said, followed the November 5, 2026, court order by Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court.
A letter to INEC with reference number ADC/NHQ/CH/2026/001, dated November 16, and stamped received by INEC same day, was anchored on a Federal High Court judgment delivered November 5 by Justice Peter Lifu of the Abuja Division in Suit No. FHC/ABJ/CS/1819/2025.
“In obedience to the said valid and subsisting judgment of the Honourable Court, I have resumed duty as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress with immediate effect,” Bala declared.
He asked INEC to acknowledge him as the authentic chairman for all official correspondence, filings and portal updates, attaching a Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment.
“Accordingly, I respectfully request the Commission to: Take formal notice of this resumption; recognise me as the National Chairman of the African Democratic Congress for all official purposes, correspondence, and filings.
“Update the Commission’s portal accordingly. A Certified True Copy of the judgement/Declaration of the Honourable Court is attached hereto for the Commission’s record and necessary action.
“I assure the Commission of my continued commitment to constitutional order, due process, and a harmonious working relationship in the interest of our democracy.”
While there was no response from INEC as at press time, the National Publicity Secretary of the ADC, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, told THISDAY that he had no comment when contacted.
